newsitem.title: JAPAN: S'tomo official says copper losses kept to minimum.
newsitem.headline: S'tomo official says copper losses kept to minimum.

text.p: Japanese trading house Sumitomo Corp kept to a minimum its losses from unauthorised deals by its former copper trading chief Yasuo Hamanaka, a Sumitomo manager said on Monday.

At the second session of Hamanaka's trial on charges of fraud and forgery, Yoshio Takeuchi of Sumitomo's credit control department rejected a suggestion that the trading house could have held the losses below the final $2.6 billion figure if it had liquidated Hamanaka's unauthorised positions more slowly.
He added that at one stage Hamanaka was asked by Sumitomo officials if he had been attempting to manipulate the world copper market, and he denied it.

During the first hearing in the trial on February 17, Hamanaka pleaded guilty to fraud and forgery in copper trades that Sumitomo said were part of a decade-long series of unauthorised deals resulting in the $2.6 billion loss.

At Monday's session one of Hamanaka's lawyers said world copper prices rose significantly after September, when Sumitomo had liquidated most of Hamanaka's positions, and asked Takeuchi if anyone at Sumitomo thought the losses would have been less if the positions had been liquidated more slowly.
"The loss was (kept to a minimum as) the result of the utmost effort by Sumitomo," Takeuchi said.
"If we had liquidated the positions more slowly, other traders would have known what our positions were and they would have rushed to go short in the market," he said.

He added that Takehiko Yonezu, an executive vice president at Sumitomo, headed a team including members of its copper trading group to liquidate unauthorised long positions taken by Hamanaka that were still open when he was fired in mid-June 1996.

Takeuchi said the team, which worked in cooperation with investment banking firm Goldman, Sachs and Co, sought to minimise the losses while maintaining order on the London Metal Exchange and completing the liquidation as quickly as possible.
Hidesato Sekine, head of Hamanaka's team of lawyers, told reporters after the session that he did not know the extent of positions left by Hamanaka when he was fired by Sumitomo.
Hamanaka, approached by reporters as he left the court room, smiled and said "no comment".
